newsitem.title: INDIA: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS - factors to watch - Sept 23.
newsitem.headline: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS - factors to watch - Sept 23.

text.p: Following are some of the main factors affecting Indian stock markets on Monday morning.
NEWS OUTLOOK:
** Indian stock markets seen volatile on fresh onslaught of political uncertainty as former prime minister P.V. Narasimha Rao resigns as president of the Congress Party over the weekend
Rao quit on Saturday after a New Delhi court ordered him to appear as a co-accused in a cheating case

** Congress party steps up the search for a chief with no clear front-runner available to take on leadership of India's oldest political organisation. Possible candidates include former cabinet minister A. K. Antony and Congress treasurer Sitaram Kesri
Congress Working Committee to meet later today to elect Rao's successor
** Rao's abrupt decision to quit the Congress presidency on Saturday hastens the decline of India's oldest party and offers Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda political breathing room, analysts say

A significant segment of Congress' 140 deputies are keen to move beyond offering simple outside support to Deve Gowda and join the government, which has pursued the same liberal economic path which Rao first blazed
"The chance of Congress participating in the Deve Gowda government is definitely brighter," says Chandan Mitra, editor of The Pioneer newspaper
** Rupee seen holding its own, but could come under pressure if the political-risk factor increases in the longer term, analysts say. It closed at 35.71/72 per dollar on Friday.

** The market capitalisation of the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) has crashed by 1,151.03 billion rupees in the last four months, the Economic Times newspaper reports, with some 50 percent of the listed stocks quoting below par
** BSE tightens margins payable in A and B group stocks. Margins will now be payable on the next day instead of on the third day, the weekend Financial Express newspaper reports
MARKETS:
** On Friday, shares across India drifted lower in sluggish trade, brokers said.
** The 30-share Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) index closed 2.99 points or 0.09 percent lower at 3346.78. The benchmark index fell 0.59 points in the week to Friday
** The 100-share National index fell 14.65 points or 0.97 percent at 1494.45
** The 50-stock National Stock Exchange index eased 0.73 points to 977.03
** The 500-share CRISIL index was off 2.42 points or 0.37 percent at 656.51
STOCKS TO WATCH:

** Chubb Corp says it enters into an agreement with Kotak Mahindra Finance Ltd to jointly develop property and casualty insurance operations in India. Terms of the deal, which both companies said they expect to benefit from, were not disclosed
** Two-wheeler maker Bajaj Auto sees drop in exports during the first four months of 1996/97 (April-March), the Economic Times reports
The firm's exports have fallen more than 27 percent to 16,190 vehicles from 22,378 units a year ago
